It was also said that the speech is complete at His words ﴿from which you flee﴾, then a new beginning is made, saying ﴿then it will meet you﴾. ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ of ugly deeds, and will recompense you for them.

Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab narrated from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Maysarah, that this verse is written in the Torah with seven hundred words, and ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah, the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ is the beginning of Surat al-Jumu'ah.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We are an unlettered nation (ummah ummiyyah); we neither write nor calculate." al-Bukhari and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah who said: "We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) when Surat al-Jumu'ah was revealed, and he recited it. When he reached ﴿and others from among them who have not yet joined them﴾, a man said to him: O Messenger of Allah, who are these who have not yet joined us? So he placed his hand upon Salman al-Farisi and said: By Him in whose hand my soul is, if faith were at the Pleiades, men from these would attain it."

Muslim also narrated it from the same narration, as a marfu' report, with the wording: "If faith were at the Pleiades, men from Persia would have taken it away," or he said: "from the sons of Persia."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Qays ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If faith were at the Pleiades, people of Persia would have attained it."

al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya' narrated from Sahl ibn Sa'd who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in the loins of the loins of the loins of men among my Companions there are men and women of my community who will enter Paradise without reckoning." Then he recited ﴿and others from among them who have not yet joined them, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills﴾ that he said: it is the religion.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated through al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from him (Ibn 'Abbas), regarding ﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah, then did not bear it﴾, that he said: they are the Jews.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated from him regarding His words ﴿asfaran﴾ that he said: books.

It is a Medinan surah.

Al-Qurtubi said: "This is the consensus of all."

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Surat al-Jumu'ah was revealed in Medina."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated the same from 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr. Muslim and the authors of the Sunan narrated from Abu Hurayrah: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite in the Friday prayer Surat al-Jumu'ah and 'When the hypocrites come to you'."

Muslim and the authors of the Sunan narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Hibban and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Jabir ibn Samurah who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the Maghrib prayer on Friday night 'Say: O disbelievers' and 'Say: He is Allah, the One', and he used to recite in the late 'Isha' prayer on Friday night Surat al-Jumu'ah and al-Munafiqun."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His words, ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah﴾. The explanation of this has already passed at the beginning of Surat al-Hadid, and of the other glorifying surahs after it. ﴿the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise﴾. The majority read these four attributes in the genitive (al-jarr), as qualifiers of Allah. It was said that they are in apposition (al-badal), but the first is preferable.

Abu Wa'il ibn Muharib, Abu al-'Aliyah, Nasr ibn 'Asim and Ru'bah read them in the nominative (al-raf') by supposing an implied subject. The majority read ﴿al-Quddus﴾ with a damma on the qaf, while Zayd ibn 'Ali read it with a fatha. Its explanation has already passed.

﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered (al-ummiyyin) a messenger from among them﴾. By al-ummiyyin is meant the Arabs, whether those among them who could write or those who could not, because they were not a people of a Book. The ummi (unlettered) in its original sense is one who neither writes nor reads what is written, and most Arabs were like this. The explanation of the meaning of ummi has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah. As for the meaning of ﴿from among them﴾: from among themselves, of their kind, and of their number. There was no tribe of the Arabs but that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had kinship with it. The point of the favour in his being from among them is that this is closer to acceptance, because a kind inclines more toward its own kind and is nearer to it.

﴿reciting to them His signs﴾, meaning the Qur'an, despite his being unlettered, who neither reads nor writes, and who learned this from no one. This clause is a qualifier of ﴿a messenger﴾. Likewise His words ﴿and purifying them﴾. Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil said: that is, He cleanses them from the filth of disbelief and sins. al-Suddi said: He takes the zakat of their wealth. It was also said: He makes them pure of heart through faith.

﴿and teaching them the Book and the wisdom﴾. This is a third qualifier of ﴿a messenger﴾. By the Book is meant the Qur'an, and by the wisdom the Sunnah, as al-Hasan said.

It was also said: the Book is writing with the pen, and the wisdom is understanding of the religion, as Malik ibn Anas said.

﴿and indeed they had been before in manifest error﴾, that is: even though before his being sent among them they were in polytheism and far from the truth.

﴿And others from among them﴾ is conjoined to ﴿the unlettered﴾, meaning: He sent among the unlettered, and He sent among others from among them ﴿who have not yet joined them﴾ at that time, and they will join them later. Or it is conjoined to the first object of ﴿teaches them﴾, meaning: and He teaches others; or to the object of ﴿purifies them﴾, meaning: He purifies them and purifies others from among them. By the others is meant whoever came after the Companions until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: by them are meant those non-Arabs who embraced Islam.

'Ikrimah said: they are the Followers (al-tabi'un).

Mujahid said: they are all people. Ibn Zayd and al-Suddi said likewise.

The clause ﴿who have not yet joined them﴾ is a qualifier of ﴿others﴾. The pronoun in ﴿from among them﴾ and ﴿them﴾ refers back to the unlettered. This supports that by the others is meant those who come after the Companions, from among the Arabs only, until the Day of Resurrection. He (ﷺ) was sent to all of mankind and jinn, but the specification of the Arabs here is for the purpose of conferring favour upon them, and that does not contradict the generality of the mission. It is also permissible that by the others is meant the non-Arabs (al-'ajam), because although they were not of the Arabs, by Islam they became of them, and all Muslims are one community, even though their races differ.

﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, that is, perfect in might and wisdom.

The demonstrative in His words ﴿that﴾ refers to what has been mentioned before.

al-Kalbi said: it means Islam.

Qatadah said: it means revelation and prophethood.

It was said: it means the joining of the non-Arabs to the Arabs. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills﴾, that is, He bestows it upon whichever of His servants He wills. ﴿And Allah is the Lord of mighty bounty﴾, which no bounty equals and nothing approaches.

﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah, then did not bear it﴾. He, glorified is He, struck a parable for the Jews who abandoned acting upon the Torah, saying: ﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah﴾, that is, were obliged to uphold it and act upon what is in it, ﴿then did not bear it﴾, that is, did not act in accordance with its requirements, nor obey what they were commanded in it, ﴿is like the likeness of a donkey carrying books﴾. Asfar is the plural of sifr, which is a large book, because it reveals (yusfiru) the meaning when it is read.

Maymun ibn Mihran said: The donkey does not know whether there is a book on its back or dung. So it is with the Jews.

al-Jurjani said: the word ḥummilū here is from al-ḥamālah in the sense of kafālah (surety), meaning they undertook (ḍaminū) the rulings of the Torah. And His words ﴿carrying﴾ are in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), or as a qualifier of the donkey, since the intended donkey is not a specific one; it is therefore in the status of an indefinite noun, as in the poet's verse:

"And I pass by the base man who abuses me, so I proceed on and say: he does not concern me."

﴿Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah﴾, that is: wretched as a likeness is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of Allah. (p-1491) The tamyiz is omitted, and the agent explained by it is implied, and ﴿the likeness of the people﴾ is the object of the dispraise. Or ﴿the likeness of the people﴾ is the agent of ﴿wretched﴾, and the object of dispraise is the relative clause following it, with an omitted modifier, meaning: the likeness of those who denied. It is also permissible that the relative clause is a qualifier of ﴿the people﴾, in which case it is in the genitive position, and the object of dispraise is omitted; the sense being: wretched is the likeness of the people who deny, is the likeness of these. ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, that is, in general terms, so the Jews enter among them by a stronger inclusion.

So Allah, glorified is He, commanded His Messenger to say to them, when they made this false claim: ﴿then wish for death﴾, so that you may pass to what you claim is your honour, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in this claim. For whoever knows that he is among the people of Paradise loves to be delivered from this abode.

The majority read ﴿fatamannaw﴾ with a damma on the waw. Ibn al-Sumayfa' read it with a fatha for lightness, and al-Kisa'i related the substitution of the waw with a hamzah.

Then Allah, glorified is He, informed that they will never do that, because of their sins, so He said: ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent ahead﴾, that is, because of what they committed of disbelief, sins, distortion and alteration. ﴿And Allah is Knower of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning in general terms, and these Jews enter among them by a stronger inclusion.

﴿So hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾. 'Ata' said: it means going and walking to the prayer.

Al-Farra' said: going forth (al-mudi), striving (al-sa'y) and going (al-dhahab) have one meaning, and this is shown by the recitation of Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud: "fa-imdu ila dhikr Allah" (so proceed to the remembrance of Allah). It was also said: what is meant is intention.

Al-Hasan said: By Allah, it is not striving on foot, but a striving of the hearts and intentions. It was said: it is action, as in His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as it should be striven for, while he is a believer﴾ [al-Isra': 19], His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾ [al-Layl: 4], and His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾ [al-Najm: 39]. Al-Qurtubi said: this is the view of the majority. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"Others came after them, striving so that they might overtake them."

And he also said:

"Striving, the two runners of Ghayz ibn Murrah, after what fell between the clan with blood."

That is: act by proceeding to the remembrance of Allah, and occupy yourselves with its means, such as washing (ghusl), ablution (wudu') and turning towards it. This view is supported by the saying of the poet:

"I strive for the greater part of the Banu Malik; every person is striving in his own affair."

﴿And leave off trade﴾, that is, abandon dealing in it, and all other dealings are included with it.

Al-Hasan said: when the caller calls on Friday, buying and selling are not lawful. The reference in His saying "that" (dhalikum) is to striving to the remembrance of Allah and leaving off trade. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿better for you﴾, that is, better for you than engaging in trade and abandoning the striving, because in compliance there is reward and recompense, and in its absence there is the lack of that, when it does not entail punishment. ﴿If you know﴾, that is, if you are among the people of knowledge, for it will not be hidden from you that this is better for you.

﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded﴾, that is, when you have performed the prayer, completed it and finished from it, ﴿disperse in the land﴾ for trade and for managing what you need of your livelihood, ﴿and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾, that is, from His provision, which He bestows upon His servants through the profits and gains that come to them in dealings. It was also said: what is meant is seeking what is with Allah of reward through performing acts of obedience and avoiding what is not lawful. ﴿And remember Allah much﴾, that is, remember Him much by thanking Him for what He has guided you to of good in the Hereafter and in this world, and likewise remember Him with what brings you closer to Him of invocations, such as praise (hamd), glorification (tasbih), magnification (takbir), seeking forgiveness (istighfar) and the like. ﴿That you may succeed﴾, that is, so that you may win the good of both abodes and attain it.

﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it and leave you standing﴾. The occasion of revelation of this verse: "The people of Medina were in poverty and need, and a caravan came from Syria while the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the khutbah (sermon) on Friday, so the people turned towards it until only twelve men remained in the mosque."

The meaning of "they rushed to it" (infadhdhu ilayha) is that they dispersed going out towards it.

Al-Mubarrad said: they inclined towards it, and the pronoun refers to trade. The pronoun was restricted to trade and not to diversion, because it was more important to them. It was also said: the sense is "when they see a trade, they rush to it, or a diversion, they rush to it," and the second was omitted because the first indicates it, as in the saying of the poet:

"We are with what we have, and you are with what you have, content; and the opinion differs."

It was also said: it referred only to the pronoun of trade, because rushing to it is blameworthy even with need for it, so how much more so rushing to diversion. Other views were also stated. ﴿And leave you standing﴾, that is, on the pulpit. Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded him to inform them that action for the Hereafter is better than action for this world, so He said: ﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade﴾, meaning the great reward, which is Paradise, ﴿better than diversion and than trade﴾, which you went towards and abandoned remaining in the mosque and hearing the sermon of the Prophet (ﷺ) for their sake. ﴿And Allah is the best of providers﴾. So seek provision from Him, and draw near to Him by acts of obedience, for that is among the means of obtaining provision and the greatest of what brings it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Hurayrah who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, why is the day called Friday?" He said: "Because in it the clay of your father Adam was gathered, and in it is the blast (of the Trumpet) and the resurrection, and at its end there are three hours, in one of which whoever calls upon Allah will have his supplication answered."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Salman who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Do you know what the day of Friday is?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said it three times, then said the third time: "It is the day on which Allah gathered your father Adam. Shall I not tell you about the day of Friday?" — the hadith.

Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best day on which the sun rises is the day of Friday. In it Adam was created, in it he was admitted into Paradise, and in it he was removed from it. The Hour will not come except on a Friday." And in the chapter there are hadiths explicitly stating that Adam was created on it.

Many hadiths have been reported concerning the virtue of the day of Friday, and likewise concerning the virtue of the Friday prayer and its great reward, and concerning the hour that is in it, and that supplication is answered in it. I have explained this in my commentary on al-Muntaqa in a way that the reader does not need anything else.

Abu 'Ubayd in his Fada'il, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif reported from Kharashah ibn al-Hurr who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab saw with me a tablet on which was written: ﴿When the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾. He said: "Who dictated this to you?" I said: "Ubayy ibn Ka'b." He said: "Indeed Ubayy is the most reciting of us of the abrogated (al-mansukh). Recite it: 'fa-imdu ila dhikr Allah' (so proceed to the remembrance of Allah)." These (compilers), except Abu 'Ubayd, reported from Ibn Umar who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, and we did not recite this verse which is in Surat al-Jumu'ah except as 'fa-imdu ila dhikr Allah'." Al-Shafi'i in al-Umm, Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also reported it from him.

They all also reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to recite "fa-imdu ila dhikr Allah," and said: "If it were 'fa-as'aw', I would run until my cloak fell off."

Abd ibn Humayd reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he recited it in the same way.

Abd ibn Humayd reported from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿So hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ that he said: "Proceed."

Abd ibn Humayd also reported from him that "sa'y" means action.

Then the verse ﴿And leave off trade﴾ was revealed, and what had been permitted before that was forbidden to them.

Ibn Jarir reported from Anas who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning His saying: ﴿Then when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾: 'It is not for the pursuit of worldly gain, but for visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother for the sake of Allah.'" Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: "You were not commanded to anything of the pursuit of this world; it is only visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother for the sake of Allah."

Then Allah revealed: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it﴾ until the end of the surah."

Abd ibn Humayd reported from Ibn Abbas regarding the verse that he said: "The caravan of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came carrying food, so they went out from the Friday prayer, some of them wanting to buy, and some wanting to look at Dihyah, and they left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing on the pulpit, and there remained in the mosque twelve men and seven women.
